questions.question_text:
The amount of rubbish produced by a town is modelled by $W=8(1.2)^{n}$, where $W$ is in tonnes and $n$ is the time in years.
What is the percentage increase each year?

options.why: Converted the whole multiplier $1.2$ to a percentage without subtracting $1$.
Converted $0.2$ to a percentage by multiplying by $10$ instead of $100$.
Used the initial amount $8$ as the percentage growth rate.

questions.solution_text:
$1.2=1+0.2$.
The amount increases by $20\%$ each year.

questions.question_text:
A scooter's value is modelled by $V=1200(0.7)^{n}$, where $V$ is in dollars and $n$ is the time in years.
What is the percentage depreciation each year?

options.why: Used the percentage of value remaining instead of the percentage lost.
Converted $0.3$ to a percentage by multiplying by $10$ instead of $100$.
Added $0.7$ to $1$ instead of subtracting $0.7$ from $1$ to find the loss.

questions.solution_text:
$0.7=1-0.3$.
The value decreases by $30\%$ each year.

questions.question_text:
A quantity is modelled by $A=150(1.6)^{x}$.
Find $A$ when $x=4$.

options.why: Multiplied $150$ by the base and then by $4$, instead of raising the base to the power $4$.
Used a power of $3$ instead of $4$, one period too few.
Used a power of $5$ instead of $4$, one period too many.

questions.question_text:
A quantity is modelled by $y=972(3)^{-x}$.
Find $y$ when $x=4$.

options.why: Divided by $3^{3}$ instead of $3^{4}$, one period too few.
Divided by $3^{5}$ instead of $3^{4}$, one period too many.
Treated the negative index as making the answer negative rather than as a reciprocal.

questions.question_text:
The number of insects is modelled by $N=9(4)^{t}$, where $t$ is the time in days.
How many insects are present after $3$ days?

options.why: Used a power of $2$ instead of $3$, one day too few.
Used a power of $4$ instead of $3$, one day too many.
Calculated $9\times4\times3$ instead of $9\times4^{3}$.

questions.question_text:
A population is modelled by $P=1800(1.2)^{t}$, where $t$ is the time in years.
Find the population after $5$ years, correct to the nearest whole number.

options.why: Used $4$ growth periods instead of $5$: $1800(1.2)^{4}=3732.48$, which rounds to $3732$.
Used $6$ growth periods instead of $5$: $1800(1.2)^{6}=5374.7712$, which rounds to $5375$.
Added the same increase of $360$ each year, calculating $1800+5\times360$ instead of repeated multiplication.

questions.question_text:
The mass of a sample is modelled by $m=300(0.8)^{t}$, where $m$ is in grams and $t$ is the time in hours.
Find the mass after $3$ hours.

options.why: Used $2$ decay periods instead of $3$, calculating $300(0.8)^{2}$.
Used $4$ decay periods instead of $3$, calculating $300(0.8)^{4}$.
Subtracted the same loss of $60$ g each hour, calculating $300-3\times60$.

questions.question_text:
The number of algae cells is modelled by $N=18(3)^{t}$, where $t$ is the time in hours.
What is the initial number of cells?

options.why: Used the base instead of the initial coefficient.
Calculated the number after $1$ hour instead of at $t=0$.
Treated $3^{0}$ as $0$ instead of $1$.

questions.solution_text:
At $t=0$, $N=18(3)^{0}=18$.
The initial number is $18$ cells.

questions.question_text:
Eric is investigating the growth in the population of a type of bacteria.
The population is modelled by $N=1000(1.6)^{t}$, where $t$ is the number of days since the start of day $1$.
How many bacteria does the model predict at the end of the $4$th day?

options.why: Applies the daily growth only once.
Adds the same $600$ bacteria each day, calculating $1000+4\times600$ instead of repeated multiplication.
Applies only three daily growth factors instead of four.

questions.solution_text:
The base $1.6$ represents a $60\%$ daily increase.
At the end of the $4$th day, $t=4$.
$N=1000(1.6)^{4}=6553.6$.
